role.altitude: The funeral director keeps talking with families, negotiating prearrangements, directing preparation and agreeing details with clergy and foreign funeral homes; looking up country rules, retyping costs into accounts, phoning suppliers and copying details between letters shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping one funeral file that feeds accounts, orders and letters
role.ambitious_version: A director whose paperwork follows from one funeral file, so more of the day goes to families.

tasks.short: Agree transport with the receiving funeral home, check the destination country's requirements, obtain permits, book the carrier, direct preparations and shipment of bodies, check the document set and send it.

steps.what: Funeral director agrees transport arrangements with the receiving funeral home abroad
Funeral director checks the destination country's document and coffin requirements
Funeral director prepares the transport permit and certificate applications: types every detail today; the deceased's details fill from the funeral file after the change
Funeral director checks each application: the deceased's details, destination and the documents attached
Funeral director submits the checked applications at the municipality and consulate and obtains the permits
Funeral director checks the carrier booking before placing it: route or flight, dates, the coffin's size and weight, and the shipper's details
Funeral director books the air or road carrier for the shipment
Funeral director directs preparation and sealing of the coffin for shipment
Funeral director checks the final document set and flight details
Funeral director sends the documents and flight details to the receiving funeral home and the family

approvals.approved_version: The document set and flight details as checked by the director in s6, addressed to the receiving funeral home and the family members named in the funeral file; any change needs a new check before sending.
Each permit and certificate application exactly as checked by the director in s3c, submitted once to the named municipality or consulate; any change needs a new check.

The carrier booking with route or flight, dates, coffin size and weight and shipper's details exactly as checked by the director in s4c, placed once with the named carrier; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The funeral software keeps a checklist per destination country with the documents, translations and coffin requirements, updated after each shipment, instead of phoning a consulate or searching old files. Carriers that take bookings for human remains online are booked there. The director checks the full document set and sends it as one package from the funeral file. Agreeing with the receiving home and directing preparation stay with the director. Permit and certificate applications fill the deceased's details from the funeral file; visits to the municipality and consulate stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Country rules were remembered or looked up each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Funeral software with per-country checklists and shared files.
tasks.still_hard: Countries whose rules change or differ by region.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a body home in time for a burial within a day.

evidence.claim: Funeral software can hold checklists and a shared funeral file.
Data protection rules apply to the relatives named, not to the deceased.

assumptions: Boundary: shipment abroad; obtaining information for legal documents (task 3334) and overseeing care of remains (task 3335) are sibling tasks.

Priced here: the answer for sibling task 3334 does not cut obtaining permits. s3 keeps 40 because application forms fill the deceased's details from the funeral file; the check and the visits to the municipality and consulate (s3s) keep their full time. s4 keeps 70 because carriers that take online bookings are booked there.
Agreeing transport, directing preparation and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of shipments abroad per year.
research_questions: Are shipments delayed by missing documents less often?

incremental.description: Funeral director updates the country checklist after each shipment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: rare destinations without a current checklist and carriers that book only by phone, so s2 keeps 85, s3 keeps 80 and s4 keeps 95 (8.0); high: regular destinations with current checklists (19.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain options and prices, record the client's wishes, discuss and negotiate prearranged funerals, prepare the contract and quote, and check and sign it with the client.

steps.what: Funeral director explains options and prices to the client
Funeral director records the client's wishes
Funeral director discusses and negotiates the prearranged funeral package and price
Funeral director prepares the prearrangement contract and quote
Funeral director checks the generated contract and quote: package, prices and terms as agreed with the client
Funeral director goes through the final contract with the client and both sign

tasks.design: The client's wishes are recorded on a wishes form in the funeral software with the options and current prices, instead of a paper form typed up later. The contract and quote are generated from the recorded wishes and the price list, and the director checks them before going through them with the client. Explaining, negotiating and signing with the client stay personal.

approvals.approved_version: The prearrangement contract and quote exactly as checked by the director in s4c, signed once by the client and the director; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Wishes were written on paper and contracts typed from them.
tasks.enabler_now: Funeral software with wishes forms and price lists.
tasks.still_hard: Clients who change their wishes over the years.
tasks.human_edge: Talking calmly about a person's own death.

reach.learn: Whether recorded wishes are clear when needed.

evidence.claim: Funeral software can generate contracts and quotes from a wishes form and price list.

assumptions: Boundary: prearranged funerals; providing information on options and maintaining the casket display (task 3337) is a sibling task.

Explaining, negotiating, the check and signing keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because the wishes are written once in the form instead of on paper and typed up later. s4 keeps 40 for adjusting the generated contract.
research_questions: Are contracts ready in the same meeting more often?

incremental.description: Funeral director keeps the price list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: clients with unusual wishes need contracts written largely by hand, so s4 keeps 70 (11.9); high: standard packages (16.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record costs per funeral, prepare, check and send the family's account, order merchandise, and reconcile payments to maintain financial records and prepare accounts.

steps.what: Funeral director records costs per funeral, including third-party costs
Funeral director prepares the family's account
Funeral director checks the final account
Funeral director sends the account to the family
Funeral director checks each merchandise order: casket, urn or cards, quantity, delivery date and the funeral it is for
Funeral director orders merchandise: caskets, urns and cards
Funeral director reconciles payments and keeps the books

approvals.approved_version: The family's account with its lines, amounts and addressee exactly as checked by the director in s3, sent once to the family member named in the funeral file; any change needs a new check before sending.
The merchandise order with item, quantity and delivery date exactly as checked by the director in s5c, placed once with the named supplier's web shop; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Each funeral has one file in the funeral software where services, merchandise and third-party costs are entered once as they are agreed, instead of collected into a spreadsheet afterwards. The family's account is generated from that file; the director checks it and sends that version. The director checks each merchandise order and places it from the file through the suppliers' web shops. A bank feed matches payments to accounts by reference. Talking with families about money stays personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs were collected afterwards and accounts typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Funeral software linked to accounting, supplier web shops and bank feeds.
tasks.still_hard: Families who split the bill or dispute costs.
tasks.human_edge: Raising an overdue account with a grieving family.
tasks.altitude: Much less typing and matching; money talks stay.

reach.learn: Whether the books are complete at year end.

evidence.claim: One funeral file feeding card, notice and condolence page ends retyping.

assumptions: Boundary: financial records and ordering; planning and coordinating funerals (task 15200) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: services and merchandise entered in the funeral file when agreed with the family under task 3332.

Checking the account and each merchandise order keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for third-party invoices still entered by hand; s2 keeps 30 for adjusting the generated account; s5 keeps 60 because web shop orders replace calls; s6 keeps 40 for payments the bank feed cannot match.
unknowns: Share of suppliers with web shops.
research_questions: Are accounts sent sooner after the funeral?

incremental.description: Funeral director keeps supplier links and the price list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many third-party invoices come on paper and payments often lack a reference, so s1 keeps 80 and s6 keeps 70 (33.6); high: costs entered once and the bank feed matches most payments (47.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask the family about faith and wishes, find an available clergy member, confirm details with them, check and send the service details, and arrange the fee to arrange for clergy members to perform services.

steps.what: Funeral director asks the family about faith and wishes for the service
Funeral director finds an available clergy member or speaker
Funeral director confirms time, place and family wishes with the clergy member
Funeral director checks the service details to send
Funeral director sends the service details and family wishes to the clergy member
Funeral director agrees the clergy fee with the clergy member
Funeral director checks the fee payment: amount as agreed, the clergy member's account and the funeral it is for
Funeral director pays the checked clergy fee

approvals.approved_version: The service details and family wishes as checked by the director in s4, addressed to the confirmed clergy member; any change needs a new check before sending.
The clergy fee with amount and account exactly as checked by the director in s6c, paid once to the named clergy member for that funeral; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: A contact list of clergy and speakers by faith, language and area, with notes on availability patterns, shortens the search a little. Talking with the family and confirming with the clergy member stay personal. The service details are filled from the funeral file into a standard message, which the director checks and sends. Arranging the fee stays with the director; recording it on the family's account is priced in task 3347 in this set.
tasks.previous_blocker: Details were retyped for each message.
tasks.enabler_now: Contact lists and messages filled from the funeral file.
tasks.still_hard: Finding clergy at short notice on weekends.
tasks.human_edge: Matching a family with a speaker who fits them.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; the people work stays.

evidence.claim: Messages can be filled from a case file instead of retyped.

assumptions: Boundary: arranging clergy; consulting families on funeral details (task 3332) is a sibling task.
s6 is agreeing the clergy fee with the clergy and keeps its full time, as do the check and payment (s6c, s6p); recording the cost on the account is cut in task 3347 in this set.
Talking with the family and the clergy keeps its full time.
unknowns: How many clergy contacts the firm uses.

incremental.description: Funeral director keeps the clergy contact list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one regular clergy contact, so the list saves almost no searching and s2 keeps 95 (3.3); high: many faiths and languages (7.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
